title: Runtime precision selector: heuristics for FP16/FP8/INT8 dispatch and on-the-fly calibration
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a runtime 'precision selector' component that chooses between FP16, FP8, and INT8 execution paths per-request and per-layer, leveraging precomputed quantization profiles and light-weight on-the-fly calibration. This ticket covers heuristics for dispatch, fallbacks when accuracy drift is detected, telemetry signals for decision-making, and integration points with the kernel dispatcher and batching layer.
acceptance_criteria: Precision selector picks FP8 or INT8 when quantization profile predicts <=0.5% top-1 quality regression vs FP16 for the active prompt distribution
Selector falls back to FP16 automatically if per-batch accuracy signal exceeds threshold or if kernel latency penalties negate cost benefits
Per-layer dispatch supported: hot layers with high sensitivity remain FP16 while quantizable layers use INT8/FP8 at runtime
End-to-end microbench harness shows expected cost reduction (>=18%) on representative workloads without exceeding quality budget
Selector exposes decision metadata in traces and console for post-hoc analysis
implementation_notes: Load quantization profiles at model-load time: include per-tensor scale maps, KL thresholds, and layer sensitivity scores
Heuristics combine static profile (offline calibration) + rolling online drift metric computed from a small validation stream sampled from production requests
Dispatch granularity: allow per-request override, per-batch decision, and per-layer mask. Default: per-batch with per-layer sensitivity masks applied.

Integrate with batching layer: ensure grouped requests share kernel compatibility (same precision) — if heterogeneous, split batch or elevate precision for entire batch based on cost/latency heuristics
Kernel interface: add 'precision_hint' in dispatch proto so backend kernels can select quantized codepath without additional model introspection
Fallback policy: on first sign of quality drift (KL divergence > 0.02 or rolling eval A/B fail), switch to conservative path (FP16) and flag offline calibration job
Maintain per-customer/route profiles for private deployments to respect data sensitivity and custom calibration results
Expose a lightweight sampling hook that inserts labeled prompts (non-customer PII) for continuous calibration when privacy policy allows
testing_plan: Create microbench suite: sequence length distribution buckets (short/med/long) and batch sizes reflecting hosted and dedicated workloads
Synthetic accuracy regression tests using held-out eval sets for each model family (LlamaX, RedLM-v2): compare FP16 baseline vs FP8/INT8 decisions
A/B rollout with Canary traffic (1%, 5%, 25%) capturing token-level divergence metrics and latency/cost delta
Chaos test: simulate kernel eviction and forced high-latency kernel to confirm selector promotes safer precision and preserves latency SLOs
E2E stress test on Dedicated pool: ensure autoscaler/reactive routing handles precision-induced throughput changes
decisions: Use hybrid static+online calibration rather than pure online to limit production noise
Default dispatch granularity set to per-batch with ability to opt-in per-layer masks for high-sensitivity layers
Quantization thresholds defined by KL divergence and observed token-accuracy delta rather than absolute SNR metrics
Prefer promoting batch precision to FP16 instead of splitting batches to avoid throughput regressions on high-frequency paths
estimated_risks: False negatives in drift detection could allow accuracy regressions to reach customers
Frequent precision switching could increase kernel churn and reduce overall throughput
Per-customer profiles add state complexity and potential config drift between control-plane and runtime
Privacy constraints may limit online sampling, reducing effectiveness of drift signals
